newsitem.title: INDIA: India forex market monthly turnover $75 bln - RBI.
newsitem.headline: India forex market monthly turnover $75 bln - RBI.

text.p: India's foreign exhange market transactions amount to around $75 billion a month, Usha Thorat, general manager of the Reserve Bank of India told a forex conference here on Sunday.
In a speech to the Forex Association of India she said dollar-rupee transactions accounted for two-thirds of the transactions, and cross-currency deals accounted for the rest.
She said transactions for importers and exporters constituted 15 percent of the total turnover.
Thorat chided some banks over dealing practices which undermine the credibility of the electronic screen based market.
"It has been observed that some banks do not update their quotes continuously; they do not deal at rates they quote on the screen and they engage in screen play," Thorat said.
"Deliberate trending of rates, knowing the other sides' position, getting brokers to reveal the interest of the counter party are unethical practices and should be eschewed," she said.
But she also praised the banks for providing two-way quotes even on days of extreme volatility and for their efforts to keep bid/offer spreads as low as possible.
Thorat said recent liberlisation measures cast a greater responsibility on the managements of banks and corporates.

She listed a number of measures introduced this year. Authorised forex dealers are allowed to fix their own limits for overnight positions and mismatches, they are allowed to initiate cross-currency positions overseas, and they are allowed to cancel and rebook cross currency options and offer derivative options to enable their customers to hedge their external liabilities.
